Android Automotive is an operating system developed by Google specifically for use in automotive infotainment systems. This skill involves understanding the platform's architecture, features, and development tools. Professionals proficient in Android Automotive can use this skill to design, develop, and optimize software applications for in-car entertainment, navigation, communication, and vehicle control functionalities, providing drivers and passengers with a connected and interactive driving experience.

Android Open Source Project (AOSP) is a development project which refers to the collaborative effort to create and maintain the open-source version of the Android operating system. It enables developers to access and modify the source code to build custom versions of Android. This skill is used to contribute to or develop tailored Android solutions by leveraging the available open-source codebase.

Zephyr RTOS is an open-source real-time operating system designed for embedded devices. It provides a scalable and secure environment for developing firmware and is suitable for applications requiring low latency and high reliability. Zephyr RTOS is used to manage hardware resources, schedule tasks, and handle communication between devices in embedded systems.

MS DOS (Microsoft Disk Operating System) refers to a command-line operating system that enables users to manage files, execute programs, and perform system operations through text-based commands. It is used to navigate the file system, run applications, and configure system settings in a direct manner. The skill encompasses knowledge of command syntax and system commands to effectively interact with the operating environment. MS DOS serves as a foundational element in understanding operating systems and computing concepts.

PC Installation involves the setup and configuration of personal computers, including hardware assembly, software installation, and peripheral device integration. This process ensures that a computer system operates efficiently by installing operating systems, drivers, and security updates. It is commonly performed in both home and enterprise environments to optimize system functionality and user experience.

Scratch Programming refers to a visual programming language designed to introduce programming concepts through interactive projects. This skill involves creating animations, games, and stories by manipulating graphical blocks that represent code structures. Knowledge of Scratch Programming is used to develop problem-solving skills and logical thinking by enabling users to design and implement their own projects in a user-friendly environment. It serves as an educational tool for learners to understand the fundamentals of coding without the complexities of traditional programming languages.

Derivative TouchDesigner is a visual development platform used for creating multimedia content, interactive installations, and live performances. It allows users to build generative and interactive projects by combining various media types such as video, audio, and 3D graphics. It is commonly used in the fields of live events, audiovisual performances, and interactive installations. As a specialized skill, proficiency in TouchDesigner requires knowledge of programming, 3D modeling, and audiovisual production.

Hacklang is a programming language developed by Facebook that is intended to be used in conjunction with the HHVM platform. It is a modern, high-level language that is designed to be both easy to use and efficient, with features such as strong typing, automatic memory management, and support for asynchronous programming. Hacklang is used by Facebook to build large-scale web applications, and it has gained popularity among developers as an alternative to PHP.

AMX Programming refers to the development of software applications using the AMX programming language, which is primarily utilized for controlling and automating audio-visual systems. This skill involves writing scripts and code to configure devices, manage user interfaces, and integrate various technologies within a networked environment. Knowledge of AMX Programming is used to enhance the functionality of AV systems, enabling seamless operation and user interaction in settings such as conference rooms, theaters, and educational institutions.

Haskell is a functional programming language that emphasizes immutability, laziness, and type safety. It is designed to allow programmers to write concise and expressive code that is easier to reason about and debug. Haskell is often used for academic research, scientific computing, and web development. It has a strong community of developers who contribute to its open source ecosystem of libraries and tools.

Elixir is a functional programming language that is compatible with the immutable and concurrent computing paradigms. Developed with the Erlang virtual machine (VM) as its basis, Elixir is designed to be scalable, fault-tolerant, and efficient for building distributed systems and web applications. The language emphasizes pure functions, pattern matching, and metaprogramming, making it well-suited for complex computations and high-performance data processing. Elixir is widely used in industries such as finance, gaming, telecommunications, and e-commerce.

Uniface is a programming language and development environment used to create scalable and mission-critical business applications. It provides a single, consistent framework for building applications that can run on different platforms and databases, making it easy to develop, deploy, and manage complex enterprise applications. Its main features include a rich set of graphical tools, programming languages, and the ability to integrate with various technologies and platforms, including web, mobile, and cloud. Uniface is widely used in the finance, healthcare, and government sectors.

Gosu is an object-oriented programming language that is specifically designed for writing applications in insurance and financial industries. It is based on Java and is known for its ease of use, flexibility, and ability to handle complex business logic. Gosu supports both dynamic and static typing and provides features such as type inference, lambdas, and data classes. It is used in a variety of applications, including web development, data analytics, and building enterprise-scale applications.

Go, also known as Golang, is an open-source programming language developed by Google. It is designed to be concise, simple, and efficient, with a focus on concurrency and scalability. Go is particularly suited for building server-side web applications, network services, and distributed systems. It has a strong type system, garbage collection, and a small runtime. Go is growing in popularity due to its ease of use, strong community support, and solid performance.

Domain-Specific Language (DSL) is a computer programming language designed for a particular domain or industry. It is focused on a specific problem or application, rather than trying to meet the needs of multiple domains. DSLs can be easier to read, write, and maintain than general-purpose programming languages, as they use familiar domain-specific terminology and structures. DSLs can increase productivity, reduce errors, and improve collaboration between domain experts and developers.

Q# is a programming language specifically designed for quantum computing. It is used to write algorithms and programs that can be executed on quantum computers or simulated on classical computers. Q# also provides libraries for building and simulating quantum circuits, as well as tools for debugging and optimizing quantum programs. It requires an understanding of quantum mechanics and quantum computing concepts.

Rust is a programming language designed for performance, security, and reliability. It offers memory safety while still providing low-level control over system resources. It is used for developing a wide range of software applications, from web services to operating systems. Rust has gained popularity among developers for its unique features and benefits.

Visual Basic is a programming language used for creating Windows applications. It is an event-driven and object-oriented language, which means it focuses on managing user interface events and objects. It is widely used in business, finance, and engineering applications due to its ease of use and quick prototyping capabilities. Skilled Visual Basic programmers can create complex software solutions with minimal effort, making it a valuable skill to have in the technology industry.

3DML refers to a markup language designed for creating and manipulating three-dimensional models and scenes. This skill encompasses the ability to define geometric shapes, materials, and lighting within a 3D environment, enabling the user to produce interactive and visually rich content. Knowledge of 3DML is utilized in various applications, including web-based 3D visualizations, gaming, and virtual reality, by facilitating the integration of 3D elements into digital platforms.

Fourth-Generation Programming Language (4GL) is a programming language that is designed to be easy to use and has a high-level of abstraction from the internal workings of the computer system. It focuses on providing faster and more efficient programming by automating many common programming tasks. 4GL is often used for database management and report generation applications. Software developers who are skilled in 4GL can design and develop software more quickly, reducing development time and costs.

Fifth-Generation Programming Languages (5GL) is a software programming language that uses natural language and graphical interfaces to create software in a more intuitive and user-friendly way. It is primarily used in the development of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and robotics. This skill requires an understanding of programming concepts, mathematical thinking, and problem-solving skills. It is essential for professionals who work in high-tech industries or research and development sectors.

APL (Programming Language) refers to a high-level programming language known for its concise syntax and powerful array manipulation capabilities. This skill involves using APL to perform complex mathematical computations, data analysis, and algorithm development efficiently. Knowledge of APL (Programming Language) is applied in fields such as finance, engineering, and scientific research, where it enables users to express operations on large datasets succinctly and effectively.

AADL is a modeling language used for the analysis, design, and implementation of software and system architectures. It provides a formalism for describing the structure and behavior of systems, including real-time and safety-critical systems. AADL models can be used to ensure that a system meets its functional and non-functional requirements, such as performance, reliability, and safety. It supports a wide range of analysis techniques, including static analysis, model checking, and simulation. AADL models are typically used in the aerospace, automotive, and avionics industries.

Advanced Business Application Programming (ABAP) refers to a programming language created by SAP for developing applications on the SAP platform. This skill involves understanding the syntax and structure of ABAP to create reports, interfaces, and enhancements that meet business requirements. Knowledge of Advanced Business Application Programming (ABAP) is utilized to customize SAP solutions, automate processes, and integrate various business functions, thereby improving operational efficiency and data management within organizations.

Augmented Backus-Naur Form (ABNF) is a formal language syntax used to describe the structure of programming languages, communication protocols, and other software systems. It is an extension of the Backus-Naur Form (BNF) notation, which uses symbols and rules to define the syntax of a language. ABNF adds additional features such as repetition, alternatives, and grouping to provide a more expressive and flexible way to describe complex syntax. It is often used in the development of software tools such as compilers, parsers, and validators.

Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) is a standard language used to describe data structures and protocol messages for communication between computer systems. It defines a syntax for expressing data structures in a platform-independent way, making it possible for systems to exchange information regardless of their hardware or software platforms. ASN.1 is used in many different fields including telecommunications, finance, healthcare, and transportation. Proficiency in ASN.1 requires knowledge of the language syntax and the ability to use it to define complex data structures and protocol messages.

ACL2 (A Computational Logic for Applicative Common Lisp) is a programming language and theorem prover used for verifying software and hardware systems. It combines the programming language Common Lisp with a proof assistant that enables developers to certify that their code meets certain properties and specifications. ACL2 is often used in safety-critical systems, such as aviation and medical devices.

Ada is a programming language that was initially designed for safety-critical applications such as aviation and military systems. It is known for its strong typing and syntax, as well as its support for concurrent programming and object-oriented programming. It is used primarily in industries that demand high reliability and safety, and has found applications in areas such as aerospace, defense, and healthcare. Ada programmers are skilled in using the language to develop complex, mission-critical software systems.

Agilent VEE is a domain-specific programming language that is used for developing test and measurement automation applications. It is widely used in the electronics industry for designing, testing, and verifying electronic products. It allows users to create and automate test procedures through a graphical user interface (GUI) without requiring extensive programming knowledge. With the help of Agilent VEE, users can automate testing equipment, acquire data, and analyze results easily and efficiently.

Android Interface Definition Language (AIDL) is a special programming language used in Android app development that allows different processes to communicate with each other through remote procedure calls (RPCs). AIDL is used to define the interface between the client and the service, and the generated interface code acts as a bridge between them, making it possible for them to communicate with each other. AIDL is particularly useful for building Android apps that require inter-process communication, such as those that use services or contain multiple components.

The Algebraic Modeling Language (AML) is a programming language specifically designed for mathematical optimization problems. AML allows users to create and model complex problems in a concise and easier-to-read format compared to more general-purpose programming languages. This skill is useful for data analysts, operations researchers, and mathematicians who work with problems involving optimization, such as maximizing profits or minimizing costs.

ALGOL (ALGOrithmic Language) is a high-level programming language designed for scientific and engineering calculations. It was developed in the late 1950s and early 1960s and has influenced the development of many other programming languages, such as Pascal and C. ALGOL uses a structured, block-structured approach to programming, allowing for easier development and maintenance of complex programs. It is primarily used in academic and research environments and is still used in some legacy systems.

Lisp is a high-level programming language with a long history and a significant impact on the development of artificial intelligence and software engineering. It is characterized by a powerful macro system, support for functional programming, and dynamic typing. Lisp is still used today in various applications, including scientific computing, natural language processing, and robotics. Familiarity with Lisp can be advantageous for developers working on complex systems and applications that require a high level of abstraction and flexibility in their design.

AmigaBASIC refers to a programming language designed for the Amiga computer platform, enabling users to create software applications and scripts. This skill encompasses understanding the syntax and commands specific to AmigaBASIC, which allows for the development of graphical user interfaces, game programming, and automation of tasks within the Amiga environment. Knowledge of AmigaBASIC is utilized to write code that interacts with the Amiga operating system and hardware, facilitating the creation of multimedia applications and enhancing user experience.

AMPL (A Mathematical Programming Language) is a high-level modeling language and software package for formulating and solving mathematical optimization problems. It is widely used in operations research, management science, and engineering to model and solve a variety of problems, such as linear and nonlinear programming, integer programming, and constraint programming, among others. AMPL provides a user-friendly interface for designing optimization models and interacting with a wide range of solvers that can be used to solve those models.

AngelScript is a scripting language primarily used in game development and software programming. It is designed to be lightweight and efficient, allowing developers to easily add custom functionality to their games and applications. It is commonly used in game engines such as Unreal Engine and Unity to create game logic and user interfaces. AngelScript supports a wide range of programming styles, including object-oriented, procedural, and functional programming. It is also cross-platform compatible, making it an ideal choice for multi-platform development projects. Overall, AngelScript is a valuable tool for software developers looking to add scripting capabilities to their projects.

App Inventor for Android is a visual programming language and development environment developed by Google that enables users to create mobile applications for Android devices without the need for extensive coding knowledge. It allows users to drag-and-drop user interface components and program logical behavior using a block-based coding approach. The software is designed for those interested in developing mobile apps and is best suited for small to mid-size projects.

Applesoft BASIC is a programming language used on the Apple II computer. It allows users to write and run BASIC programs for various purposes, such as games, educational software, and small business applications. This specialized skill requires knowledge of programming fundamentals, syntax, and logic.

Arbortext Command Language (ACL) is a programming language used to automate tasks within the Arbortext publishing software suite. It allows users to create scripts to perform tasks such as importing, exporting, and modifying content. ACL can also be used to create custom templates and stylesheets, and to interface with other software tools. A strong understanding of programming principles and experience working with Arbortext are necessary to effectively use ACL.

ARC Macro Language (AML) is a programming language created for use in the ArcGIS geographic information system software. It is used to automate repetitive tasks, develop custom functions and tools, and create batch processes for GIS data analysis and management. AML is proprietary and specific to the ArcGIS software, therefore it requires licensing and training to use effectively.

ASIC Programming Language refers to a set of programming languages specifically designed for the development of Application-Specific Integrated Circuits. This skill involves understanding hardware description languages that enable the design, simulation, and verification of digital circuits tailored for specific applications. Knowledge of ASIC Programming Language is used to create efficient and optimized hardware solutions by translating high-level specifications into low-level implementations that meet performance and power requirements.

Abstract State Machine Language (ASML) is a formal modeling language used for specifying the behavior of software systems. ASML describes systems using a set of states and transitions between them, providing a concise and precise way to represent complex software behavior. As a specialized skill, proficiency in ASML allows programmers to create more reliable, verifiable software systems by applying formal methods to their design and implementation processes.

Assembly language is a low-level programming language that is specific to a particular computer architecture. It involves writing instructions in machine-readable code that can be directly executed by the computer's CPU. Assembly language requires a deep understanding of computer hardware and microarchitecture, and is used to optimize performance-critical software such as device drivers, firmware, and operating system kernels. Due to its complexity and specificity, it is generally not used for general-purpose programming tasks.

Atari BASIC is a programming language developed for the Atari 8-bit family of computers. It allows users to create and run programs on these computers, and is used primarily for game development and other types of software development. It includes a variety of features and commands specific to the Atari computer platform, making it a specialized skill for those interested in programming for these machines.

AviSynth is a scripting language and framework for video post-production that allows users to create and manipulate video files through a series of commands. This skill involves writing scripts that can perform tasks such as filtering, resizing, and combining video clips, enabling precise control over the editing process. Knowledge of AviSynth is utilized to enhance video quality, apply effects, and automate repetitive editing tasks, making it a valuable tool for video editors and enthusiasts.

Knowledge of IBM Basic Assembly Language And Successors is used to develop system software, optimize performance, and troubleshoot hardware-related issues by providing precise control over system resources.

BASIC Stamp is a microcontroller and programming language that requires specialized knowledge to use. It is typically used for projects that require precise control and automation, such as robotics and home automation. The programming language is similar to BASIC, but it is designed specifically for use with microcontrollers. Learning how to use BASIC Stamp requires time and effort, but it can be a valuable skill for anyone interested in electronics and automation.

Blitz BASIC is an object-oriented programming language that is commonly used in game development. It allows developers to create games and other interactive applications with ease, using a syntax that is easy to understand and use. With its powerful features and intuitive interface, Blitz BASIC is a valuable skill for anyone looking to create engaging software applications.

Turbo Pascal refers to an integrated development environment and compiler for the Pascal programming language, designed to facilitate software development. This skill encompasses knowledge of programming concepts, syntax, and debugging techniques specific to Turbo Pascal, enabling the user to create, compile, and execute applications efficiently. Understanding Turbo Pascal is utilized in educational settings and for developing applications that require structured programming and data management.

C# is a programming language used to develop a variety of applications, including desktop, web, and gaming applications, as well as mobile apps for iOS and Android. It is commonly used in Microsoft's .NET framework and is known for its simplicity, powerful capabilities, and widespread use in the software industry. C# developers are in demand and can expect to earn competitive salaries.

Client/Server Application Language (C/AL) refers to a programming language used primarily for developing applications in a client-server architecture, particularly within Microsoft Dynamics NAV. This skill involves writing code that enables the creation, modification, and management of business logic and data processing in enterprise resource planning systems. Knowledge of Client/Server Application Language (C/AL) is utilized to implement custom functionalities, automate processes, and enhance user interfaces, thereby improving overall system performance and user experience.

Citect Cicode is a programming language used to create automated processes and applications for industrial control systems using CitectSCADA software. It allows for the creation of custom functions, graphical user interfaces, and communication protocols to connect with various devices and systems. This specialized skill is important for professionals working in the field of automation and control systems.

Clarify Clearbasic refers to the process of simplifying and elucidating the Clearbasic programming language, which is designed for creating applications with a focus on clarity and ease of use. This skill involves understanding the syntax, structure, and functionalities of Clearbasic to enhance comprehension and facilitate effective coding practices. Knowledge of Clarify Clearbasic is utilized to improve code readability, streamline development processes, and assist users in troubleshooting and optimizing their programming tasks.

Climacs is an extensible text editor written in Common Lisp. It is designed for programmers and developers who require advanced editing functionalities such as syntax highlighting, code folding, and macro support. Its architecture makes it easy to customize and add new features, making it highly adaptable to different programming languages and project requirements. It is also highly configurable, allowing users to tailor the interface and editor commands to their own preferences.

CLISP is an implementation of the Common Lisp programming language that offers an interactive environment for programming and development. It supports several features, including dynamic loading of modules, garbage collection, and CLOS, a Common Lisp Object System. It is also portable and compatible with various operating systems, including Unix, Windows, and macOS. CLISP is often used for developing Lisp applications, scripting, and for rapid prototyping.

CLIST (Control Language Interpretive System) is a programming language used for writing scripts and macros for IBM mainframes. It is used to automate repetitive tasks, manage job schedules, and perform system operations on mainframe computers. CLIST programming involves creating command sequences that automate and control various mainframe system functions. This specialized skill is primarily used by mainframe programmers and administrators.

Clojure is a modern, general-purpose programming language that emphasizes functional programming and is designed to be simple, concise, and efficient. It is particularly well-suited for concurrent and parallel programming, and encourages immutability and simplicity in code. Clojure runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) and can also be compiled to JavaScript, making it a versatile choice for web and mobile applications, as well as backend services.

Common Lisp Object System (CLOS) is a programming language extension that allows developers to create and manipulate objects in Common Lisp. CLOS is based on the concept of classes and objects, and provides a flexible and dynamic approach to object-oriented programming. It is known for its support of multiple inheritance, method combination, and generic functions. Skill with CLOS is useful for developing complex applications that require a robust and flexible object-oriented programming approach.

CoffeeScript is a programming language that compiles to JavaScript, which allows developers to write more concise and readable code while still being able to run it in a web browser. It is used primarily for front-end web development and can be used in conjunction with popular frameworks and libraries such as Node.js and AngularJS. Some of the benefits of using CoffeeScript include easier maintenance, faster development time, and improved readability of code.

PowerHouse is a programming language and integrated development environment (IDE) used for building business applications, particularly in the finance, manufacturing, and distribution industries. PowerHouse was created by Cognizant Technology Solutions and is known for its ability to handle large amounts of data and its performance efficiency. It uses a proprietary programming language called "PowerHouse 4GL" and has a range of features to help developers build and maintain applications, including a form designer, report writer, and data dictionary.

Common Language Infrastructure (CLI) is an open standard that defines a platform-independent executable code and runtime environment for software development. It allows for interoperability between different programming languages and enables the execution of code on different operating systems and hardware architectures. CLI includes features such as memory management, exception handling, and security, making it a useful tool for developers building complex, cross-platform applications. A knowledge of CLI is essential for developers working with .NET framework and related technologies.

A Common Type System (CTS) is a set of data types and rules used for data interchange between different programming languages and platforms. It provides a universal standard for representing data and allows programs written in different languages to communicate with each other seamlessly. Understanding CTS is essential for software developers who work on different platforms and need to ensure that their applications can interoperate with other systems.

Component Pascal is a programming language that is related to the Pascal family of languages. It was developed to support the construction of complex software systems using object-oriented concepts and reusable software components. It features a syntax that is similar to Pascal, but with extensions for object-oriented programming, such as classes, interfaces, and inheritance. Component Pascal is used mainly for development of software applications and systems in various industries, such as telecommunications, healthcare, finance, and manufacturing.

CPython is the standard implementation of the Python programming language. It is an open-source project, written in C and Python, and is maintained by the Python Software Foundation. CPython is widely used and well-documented, and is compatible with numerous third-party libraries and tools. It is an essential tool for Python developers and is often used as a platform for creating Python-based applications, frameworks, and tools.

DarkBASIC is a programming language specifically designed for creating real-time 3D games and applications for Windows. It provides an easy-to-use, high-level syntax that makes game development accessible to beginners, while also offering advanced features for more experienced programmers. DarkBASIC includes a range of game development tools and libraries, allowing users to create complex games and simulations with minimal coding.

Data Manipulation Language (DML) refers to a category of SQL (Structured Query Language) commands used for managing and manipulating data within a database. It includes commands such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE, which allow users to retrieve, add, modify, and remove data from database tables. DML is essential for performing data operations in database systems, enabling users to interact with and modify data according to their requirements.

Race Condition is a programming concept where the outcome of a code execution depends on the sequence or timing of events. It requires specialized skills and experience in programming to identify and prevent race conditions, as they can lead to unpredictable or incorrect program behavior. Developers need to be cautious in handling and accessing shared resources and design programs that can synchronize and coordinate concurrent operations to avoid race conditions.

Datalog refers to a declarative programming language that is primarily used for querying and manipulating databases. This skill involves the use of logical rules and facts to derive conclusions and answer complex queries efficiently. Knowledge of Datalog is applied in areas such as knowledge representation, data integration, and reasoning tasks, enabling users to express queries in a clear and concise manner while leveraging the underlying logical structure of the data.

The Decorator pattern is a design pattern used in object-oriented programming that allows behavior to be added to an individual object, either statically or dynamically, without affecting the behavior of other objects from the same class. It is used to extend or modify the functionality of objects at runtime by wrapping them in an object of a decorator class that encapsulates the original object's behavior, and adds new methods or behaviors to the wrapped object.

DIBOL (Digital Interactive Business Oriented Language) is a programming language used in business applications. It was developed by Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC) in the 1970s and is similar to COBOL. DIBOL has features that allow for easy handling of business data and reports, making it useful in finance, inventory management, and other administrative tasks. While DIBOL is no longer widely used, some legacy systems still rely on it, and there are still developers with expertise in the language.

Markup languages are languages that are used to format and structure text. They include HTML, XML, and Markdown. Markup languages are commonly used in website development and content management systems. Proficiency in markup languages involves the knowledge of the syntax, vocabulary, and best practices for creating and editing structured content. This skill is essential for web developers, content creators, and digital marketers.

Double Dispatch is a programming technique used in object-oriented languages that allows two objects to communicate with each other and execute specific operations based on their types. It involves calling a method on one object, which then decides which method to call on another object based on its type. This technique is often used to achieve polymorphism and to better manage complex software systems. It requires a good understanding of object-oriented programming principles and is considered a specialized skill.

Racket is a high-level programming language designed to support functional and imperative programming paradigms. It is a dialect of the Lisp language, and its syntax is based on S-expressions. Racket includes an extensive library of built-in functions and data structures, making it ideal for various applications, including web development, game development, and scientific computing. Its development environment, DrRacket, provides an integrated development environment (IDE) with features such as syntax highlighting, code completion, and debugging tools.

SKILL_NAME: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code (EBCDIC)
SKILL_DESCRIPTION: EBCDIC is a character encoding used mainly on IBM mainframe and AS/400 computers. It is different from the more commonly used ASCII encoding and requires specialized skills to work with. EBCDIC uses 8 bits to represent each character and assigns unique codes to letters, numbers, and symbols. Programmers who work with legacy mainframe systems may require expertise in EBCDIC to manipulate and understand data stored in this encoding.

Extended Backus Naur Form (EBNF) is a metalanguage used for defining the syntax of programming languages, command languages, document formats, and other formal languages. It consists of a set of rules that describe the structure of a language, with each rule specifying how certain elements can be combined to form valid expressions. EBNF is commonly used by computer scientists, linguists, and software developers to create formal specifications of languages and to communicate those specifications to others. As a specialized skill, it requires a good understanding of grammatical structure and a working knowledge of programming languages.

G Programming Language refers to a high-level programming language primarily used for developing applications in the field of measurement and automation. This skill encompasses the ability to create and manipulate graphical user interfaces, manage data acquisition, and control hardware devices. Knowledge of G Programming Language is utilized to design and implement software solutions that facilitate efficient data processing and system control in various engineering and scientific applications.

Emacs Lisp is a programming language used for extending and customizing the Emacs text editor. It allows users to write scripts and programs to automate tasks, enhance functionality, and modify the behavior of Emacs. With Emacs Lisp, users can create custom commands, define new features, and tailor Emacs to suit their specific needs and preferences, making it a powerful tool for efficient text editing and workflow optimization.

Embeddable Common Lisp (ECL) is a software library that allows Common Lisp programs to be embedded into other programs or used as a standalone application. It provides a complete Common Lisp environment and can be used as a scripting language within other software applications. ECL is designed to be highly portable and works on a variety of platforms, including Linux, macOS, Windows, and iOS. It is used in a variety of fields, including scientific computing, artificial intelligence, and web development. To use ECL effectively, one must have knowledge of Common Lisp programming language.

Embedded Domain-Specific Languages (EDSLs) is a software development approach that involves creating mini-languages to solve specific problems within a particular domain. These languages are tailored to meet the unique needs and requirements of a specific application, and they often provide a more concise and readable syntax for developers to follow. EDSLs are typically embedded within an existing programming language, making it possible to create custom-built solutions that integrate more seamlessly with the existing codebase. This specialized skill requires an in-depth knowledge of programming languages and the ability to design and implement EDSLs that align with the goals of the project.

Eltron Programming Language refers to a programming language designed for developing applications within the Eltron ecosystem. This skill involves understanding its syntax, data structures, and libraries, which enable the creation of software solutions tailored to specific functionalities. Knowledge of Eltron Programming Language is utilized to implement algorithms, manage data flow, and integrate with other systems, facilitating efficient application development and maintenance.

Esterel is a specialized software language used for developing reactive systems. It is used in safety-critical industries such as aviation, automotive, and medical systems. Esterel has a formal semantics and allows for mathematical reasoning about the correctness of the system. It uses synchronous programming, where all inputs are processed at specific time instants, and can handle a combination of hardware and software interactions. Esterel is often used in conjunction with other languages, such as C or VHDL.

Unified Expression Languages is the ability to effectively use programming languages such as Java Expression Language (JEL), JSP Expression Language (EL), and Unified EL (UEL) for efficient software development. This skill involves the ability to write clear and concise expressions for data manipulation, validation, and flow control. It also includes understanding how to integrate these languages into various frameworks and tools like JSF, Struts, and Spring. Unified Expression Languages are essential for developing scalable and maintainable software applications.

F# is a functional programming language that is designed to run on the .NET framework, making it ideal for developing Windows applications or web services. It is based on the ML family of languages and incorporates features such as pattern matching, type inference, and immutable data structures. F# is commonly used in financial modeling, data sciences, and scientific computing. Programmers with expertise in F# are in demand for developing complex software solutions.

Fortran is a programming language developed for scientific and engineering calculations. It simplifies complex mathematical computations and makes it easier to write code for scientific analysis. Fortran has been in use for several decades and is still widely used today in fields like weather forecasting, computational fluid dynamics, and nuclear physics. Those with a Specialized Skill in Fortran are adept at programming in the language and can help organizations in various industries optimize their scientific computing processes.

Forth is a high-level programming language that is particularly suited to embedded and real-time systems. It is a stack-based language, meaning that it operates on data stored on a stack. Forth is designed for efficiency, modularity, and low-level hardware control, and is commonly used in applications such as robotics, industrial automation, and microcontrollers. It is a flexible and customizable language that can be tailored to specific hardware and software requirements, making it a valuable tool for developers working in these areas.

Visual FoxPro refers to a data-centric programming language and environment that is used for developing database applications. This skill encompasses the ability to design, create, and manage databases, as well as to develop user interfaces and reports. Knowledge of Visual FoxPro is utilized to build applications that facilitate data manipulation, retrieval, and reporting, enabling efficient management of information in various business contexts.

Free Pascal is a free and open-source compiler for the Pascal and Object Pascal programming languages. It allows developers to write code and create applications for a variety of platforms, including Windows, Linux, macOS, and more. As a specialized skill, proficiency in Free Pascal can be useful for those interested in developing software in the Pascal/Object Pascal languages.

IBM Generalized Markup Language (GML) is an early markup language used to define document structures and their formatting. It was developed by IBM in the 1960s and was widely used in the publishing industry before the rise of more modern markup languages such as HTML and XML. GML is based on a hierarchical structure of nested elements and allows for the definition of various formatting options such as fonts, styles, and sizes.

Gforth refers to an implementation of the Forth programming language, designed for high performance and extensibility. This skill encompasses the ability to write and execute programs using a stack-based approach, enabling efficient manipulation of data and control structures. Knowledge of Gforth is used to develop applications in embedded systems, scripting, and rapid prototyping by leveraging its interactive environment and extensible nature for custom functionality.

Glasgow Haskell Compilers refers to a suite of tools designed for compiling programs written in the Haskell programming language. This skill encompasses understanding the compilation process, optimization techniques, and code generation that enable efficient execution of Haskell applications. Knowledge of Glasgow Haskell Compilers is used to develop software that leverages functional programming principles, ensuring performance and correctness in various computing environments.

The OpenGL Shading Language (GLSL) is a high-level language used to create shaders that run on graphics processing units (GPUs). These shaders are responsible for rendering objects and scenes in 3D graphics applications. GLSL provides a flexible and powerful toolset for creating shaders that can handle a wide range of effects, from simple color changes to complex lighting and shadowing effects. GLSL programming requires knowledge of computer graphics, geometry, and mathematics, and is typically used by game developers, graphic designers, and other professionals in the field of computer graphics.

Dart is an open-source, object-oriented, general-purpose programming language developed by Google. It is fast, efficient, and easy to learn, and it's particularly suited for building web and mobile applications. Dart has a syntax that is similar to those of other programming languages such as C++, Java, and JavaScript, making it easy for developers to pick up. With its reliable garbage collection, Dart allows developers to build high-performance applications quickly and efficiently. Its versatility makes it an attractive choice for companies looking to create complex applications that are both scalable and user-friendly.

Visual Programming Language (VPL) is a software tool that allows developers to create code using graphical elements instead of traditional text-based coding. It is specifically designed to make coding easier and more accessible for non-programmers or those with limited coding experience. VPLs usually offer drag-and-drop functionality, allowing the creator to visually arrange blocks of code to create programs. This skill is relevant to software developers, designers, and other technology professionals interested in developing expertise in VPLs.

GW-BASIC is an early programming language developed by Microsoft in the 1980s. It was used for simple applications and programming tasks and was popular among hobbyists and beginner programmers at the time. The language has since been surpassed by more advanced programming languages and is no longer widely used today. However, some software and systems developed using GW-BASIC may still be in use.

Haxe is a high-level, cross-platform programming language designed for creating web, desktop, and mobile applications. It allows developers to write code once and deploy it to multiple platforms, including iOS, Android, Windows, and Linux. Haxe is known for its flexibility, performance, and ease of use, and it is often used to create complex applications for companies and organizations of all sizes. As a specialized skill, Haxe requires a deep understanding of programming concepts and best practices, as well as experience with related tools and frameworks.

IBM High Level Assembler (HLASM) is a software tool used for program development on IBM mainframes. It allows programmers to write assembly language code in a high-level format, rather than using low-level machine language. HLASM supports a wide range of features, including conditional assembly, macro processing, and data manipulation. It is commonly used in the development of system-level software, such as operating systems and compilers.

HP BASIC is a programming language developed by Hewlett-Packard that is used to create and run programs for the HP 3000 and HP 9000 series of computers. It is a high-level language that is easy to learn and use, making it a popular choice for developing business applications, database systems, and other software solutions. It is also highly versatile, allowing programmers to write code for a wide range of hardware platforms and operating systems. HP BASIC has been around for decades and is still widely used today, especially in legacy systems and applications.

Rocky Mountain BASIC is a programming language often used for scientific and engineering applications. It was originally developed for mainframe computers in the 1970s but has since been adapted to work on modern computers. It is known for its ease of use and is still widely used in certain industries. Being skilled in Rocky Mountain BASIC may be useful for individuals seeking employment in scientific or engineering fields.

HyperTalk is a programming language that was used in the HyperCard software, which was popular in the late 1980s and early 1990s. It allowed users to create their own programs and applications without having to learn complex coding languages. HyperTalk is still used by some developers today for its simplicity and ease of use.

IBM RPG (Report Program Generator) is a programming language used in IBM iSeries or AS/400 systems for developing business applications. It is designed for efficient handling of large databases and has features that facilitate the development of complex applications. RPG uses a fixed format syntax, with statements for defining data structures, manipulating data, making decisions, and controlling program flow. It also includes built-in database access functions and supports integration with other programming languages like Java and PHP. RPG developers are in demand for their ability to create robust, scalable, and secure applications for enterprise-level business operations.

Iconv is a command-line tool used to convert between different character encodings. It is commonly used in programming and web development to ensure that text is displayed correctly across different platforms and languages. Iconv can convert text between a wide range of encodings, including ASCII, Unicode, and foreign language character sets. It requires specialized knowledge in Unicode and character encoding to use effectively.

IDEF is a standardized methodology used for modeling and documenting systems and processes. It is commonly used in software development to help stakeholders understand and communicate the design and functionality of a system. The methodology consists of a set of techniques and tools for capturing and analyzing information, and organizing it into diagrams, flowcharts, and other visual representations. IDEF can help ensure that all members of a development team are on the same page and that project requirements are met.

Interactive Data Language (IDL) is a programming language and environment used in remote sensing, astronomy, and other scientific fields to process and analyze large datasets. It offers tools for statistical analysis, image processing, and visualization, and is commonly used for data exploration, modeling, and simulation. IDL is especially useful for working with multidimensional arrays and large datasets, and is often used in conjunction with other programming languages and software packages.

Iterators is a computer programming concept that allows developers to traverse a sequence or collection of data in a specific order, accessing each element one at a time. It helps simplify code and improve performance by eliminating the need to load an entire collection into memory. Skilled programmers can use iterators to write efficient, flexible, and reusable code.

SAS/IML is a specialized software skill focused on the SAS Interactive Matrix Language, which is a powerful data processing and analysis tool used in statistics and data science. It enables users to manipulate and analyze large datasets, automate repetitive tasks, and create custom procedures for statistical modeling and simulation. SAS/IML is particularly useful for data manipulation, statistical modeling, and simulation tasks in finance, healthcare, and other industries where large and complex datasets are present.

IBM Informix-4GL is a high-level programming language designed for business applications. It is part of the IBM Informix database software and enables developers to create fast and reliable applications for various industries, including finance, healthcare, and retail. It is known for its ease of use and its ability to handle complex data structures and relationships. This specialized skill requires knowledge of programming concepts, database management, and SQL.

Inline Assembler is a specialized software programming skill that involves inserting snippets of assembly code within high-level language code. It allows programmers to optimize critical sections of code and leverage the low-level functionality of the processor directly, improving the performance and efficiency of the program. Inline Assembler requires knowledge of assembly language, processor architecture, and the ability to bridge the gap between high-level and low-level programming languages.

Inline Function is a programming technique where the code of a function is inserted directly into the code where the function is called, instead of calling it as a separate instruction. This technique is used for improving the efficiency of the program, reducing function call overheads, and optimizing the code. The skillset required for implementing inline functions includes proficiency in programming languages, understanding of the software architecture, and familiarity with the compiler and debugging tools.

X86 Assembly Language is a low-level programming language used for writing software that interacts directly with a computer's hardware. It requires a deep understanding of computer architecture and binary code. Programmers who have expertise in X86 Assembly Language can develop efficient and high-performance software, including operating systems, drivers, and embedded systems.

J Sharp refers to a programming language that is designed to provide a modern and efficient way to develop applications on the .NET framework. This skill encompasses the ability to write, compile, and execute code that integrates seamlessly with other .NET languages, enabling developers to create robust software solutions. Knowledge of J Sharp is used to implement object-oriented programming principles, manage data structures, and develop user interfaces, thereby enhancing application functionality and performance.

JOVIAL stands for "Jules Own Version of the International Algorithmic Language" and is a high-level programming language that is used primarily for developing real-time embedded systems for defense applications. It was developed by the United States Air Force in the 1950s and is known for its reliability, safety, and security features. JOVIAL is still used today in various defense and aerospace applications. Programmers with expertise in JOVIAL are in high demand in the defense industry.

KM Programming Language refers to a programming language designed for knowledge management applications, facilitating the organization, retrieval, and sharing of information. This skill encompasses the ability to create and manipulate data structures that support knowledge representation and reasoning. Knowledge of KM Programming Language is used to develop systems that enhance decision-making processes, improve collaboration, and streamline information workflows within organizations.

Scheme is a general-purpose programming language that emphasizes functional programming and minimalist design. It is a dialect of Lisp and was designed to have a simple syntax and to be easy to learn and use. Scheme is often used in education, artificial intelligence research, and embedded systems programming. Its key features include lexical scoping, first-class continuations, and the ability to define macros.

B is a programming language developed by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie in 1970. It is a precursor to the popular C programming language and was designed for use on the Unix operating system. B is a low-level language that allows for direct access to hardware, making it useful for system programming tasks. Although it is no longer widely used, B was an important step in the development of modern programming languages and operating systems.

Lattice C is a programming language and development environment used for developing software on embedded systems and other low-level hardware platforms. It is known for its ability to produce highly optimized code and its support for a wide range of hardware architectures. Developing software using Lattice C requires specialized knowledge and skills in computer programming and hardware design.

LC-3 is a low-level computer programming language used for developing operating systems, compilers, and other system software. It is widely used in the field of computer engineering and is particularly popular in academic and research settings. Mastering LC-3 requires a deep understanding of computer hardware and architecture and is thus considered a specialized skill.

Low-Level Programming Language refers to programming languages that provide little abstraction from a computer's hardware, allowing direct manipulation of memory and system resources. This skill encompasses understanding the architecture of computer systems and the specific instructions that a processor can execute. Knowledge of Low-Level Programming Language is used to develop system software, embedded systems, and performance-critical applications by enabling efficient resource management and optimization of hardware interactions.

Magik is an object-oriented programming language and platform used in software development for building enterprise-level applications. It is commonly utilized in the manufacturing, finance, and telecommunications industries. Magik is known for its built-in support for data modeling, interprocess communication, and distributed systems. It also offers features such as garbage collection, exception handling, and memory management.

Market Data Definition Language (MDDL) is a programming language used in the financial industry to standardize the representation of market data across different systems and platforms. It allows for the easy exchange and comparison of financial data between different vendors and applications. As a specialized skill, proficiency in MDDL requires expertise in data modeling and programming languages, and is often a requirement for certain roles in finance and software development.

QBasic is a programming language and software that allows users to create simple programs and games using a basic syntax. It was popular in the 1990s as an entry-level programming tool for beginners, and is still used by some hobbyists and educators today. QBasic is known for its simplicity and user-friendliness, making it a good tool for learning programming fundamentals.

QuickBASIC is a legacy programming language and development environment that was widely used in the 1980s and 1990s for developing DOS-based applications, including games and business software. It was popular for its simplicity and ease-of-use, making it accessible to novice programmers. It has since been largely superseded by more modern languages and environments, but some developers and enthusiasts continue to use it for certain applications. Skills related to QuickBASIC would involve knowledge of its syntax and programming constructs, as well as the ability to write and debug programs using the QuickBASIC development environment.

Visual Basic .NET is a programming language used for developing Windows applications and other programs. It is an object-oriented language that is easy to learn and use, with a syntax similar to natural language. VB.NET allows developers to create user interfaces, manipulate data, and interact with other software applications. It also supports the creation of web applications and services using the .NET framework. proficiency in VB.NET is beneficial for software developers, engineers, and programmers who work with Windows applications or software development.

Microsoft Visual Programming Language, also known as Visual Basic (VB), is a high-level programming language designed by Microsoft for developing Windows applications. It allows developers to create user-friendly graphical interfaces by using a drag-and-drop interface builder and a variety of pre-built controls. VB is an object-oriented language that supports event-driven programming and can be used to develop a wide range of applications, from simple desktop utilities to complex enterprise-level software. It is an important tool for developers working with the Microsoft .NET Framework and is widely used for creating desktop, web, and mobile applications.

Microsoft Interface Definition Language (MIDL) is a programming language used to create interfaces between different software components, allowing them to communicate with each other. It is commonly used in building distributed systems and is an essential tool for developers working with Microsoft technologies. MIDL is used to define interfaces between different components of a system, such as application programming interfaces (APIs), components of an operating system or distributed computing components. It is necessary for developers to have a good understanding of MIDL in order to build effective and reliable software systems.

MIPS Instruction Set refers to a set of instructions used in MIPS architecture, which is a type of computer architecture that employs a reduced instruction set computing design. This skill encompasses understanding the various operations, data types, and addressing modes defined by the MIPS architecture, enabling efficient programming and optimization of software applications. Knowledge of the MIPS Instruction Set is utilized in developing assembly language programs, performing low-level hardware interactions, and enhancing performance in embedded systems and computer engineering projects.

MIPS64 is a specialized instruction set architecture used in high-performance computing and embedded systems. It is designed for 64-bit processors and offers superior performance and efficiency compared to other architectures. Developing software for MIPS64 requires specialized skills and knowledge of the unique features and characteristics of the architecture.

PL/I (Procedural Programming Language) is a high-level programming language designed for creating applications in a variety of fields, including scientific, engineering, and business environments. This skill supports procedural, structured, and modular programming, enabling the development of complex software systems with clear, maintainable code. The language is used for tasks that require efficient handling of data processing, file management, and mathematical computations, making it suitable for large-scale and multi-purpose software projects.

ModeliCA is a specialized software skill that involves using the ModeliCA language to create models of complex systems in various industries such as automotive, aerospace, and telecommunications. It is a modeling language that enables engineers to create and simulate dynamic models of physical systems in a more efficient and effective manner. The skill involves knowledge of both modeling concepts and the ModeliCA language. It is a valuable skill for professionals in the fields of engineering and computer science.

Modeling Languages is a software skill that involves the use of specialized languages to create models of systems, processes, or structures. These models represent the behavior and structure of the system or process, helping software developers and engineers to design, analyze, and optimize software applications. Annual Salary Increase Process refers to the systematic approach organizations use to evaluate and implement salary adjustments for employees on an annual basis. Evaluating staff is a crucial skill for managers and supervisors to assess employee performance, identify areas for improvement, and provide feedback to motivate and retain top talent. Productivity Management refers to the systematic approach to optimizing efficiency and effectiveness in work processes and resource utilization. Knowledge of Productivity Management is used to streamline operations, improve time management, and foster a culture of continuous improvement within organizations.

Futuretask refers to a strategic approach that involves planning and prioritizing tasks to achieve long-term goals and objectives. Accredited Community Manager is a professional certification that recognizes expertise in managing online communities. Professional Administrative Certification of Excellence (PACE) is a certification program that validates and recognizes the competence and proficiency of administrative professionals in various industries.
